settings.title: AFFORDABLE Nil T2 Filing for Real Estate Holding Corporations

settings.editor:
Property sitting in a corporation still generates a filing obligation every year: title in the corporation name, a property tax bill whether or not anything is built, and a return owed for as long as the entity exists. A holding, rental or investment corporation is not nil in any year it earns, so we test each year before charging for it, and the idle ones are $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

Whether the corporation holds land banked against a build that has not started, a parcel rolled in before a plan changed, a future cottage, or a development site left untouched for years, we check rent and carrying costs first, add Schedule 8 where a building stands on the land, and transmit the return electronically. Any year with rent in it goes to the full service.

settings.title: When a Real Estate Holding Corporation Is Not Nil

settings.description_text: A corporation receiving rent for any part of the year is a rental corporation for that year, and a rental corporation is not nil.
Property tax, insurance or mortgage interest paid out of the corporation is an expense, and an expense is activity.
A sale, a transfer to a shareholder or a partial disposition puts a capital gain or loss in that year.

settings.title_text: A Deposit or Option Fee Arrived
settings.description_text: Money taken on a future sale is received by the corporation, whether or not the deal ever closes.

settings.editor:
Carrying costs defeat more of these years than rent does. Property tax falls due annually whether or not anything is built, and the question is only which entity paid it. Where the corporation paid, the year has an expense on Schedule 125 and is an ordinary return. Where the shareholder paid personally, the corporation may genuinely have had a year with nothing in it at all.

An earning or spending year is a full T2, prepared by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca for $350.00 plus HST per year. A year in which the land simply sat, costing the corporation nothing, is filed on this page at $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

settings.title: Which T2 Schedules a Real Estate Holding Corporation Files

settings.editor:
ScheduleWhat it reportsOn a nil yearWhy
Schedule 100Balance sheet informationRequiredLand and buildings sit on the balance sheet at cost, with any mortgage against them, so it is never an empty schedule.
Schedule 125Income statement informationRequiredReports nil rental revenue and nil carrying costs for a year the corporation neither collected nor paid.
Schedule 141Notes checklistRequiredGoes with Schedules 100 and 125 and names whoever compiled them.
Schedule 50Shareholder informationRequiredProperty is often held by two or more family members or partners. Anyone at 10% or more of a class is named.
Schedule 24First-time filer informationFirst return onlyFiled with the first T2 after incorporation, which is often the year the property was bought.
Schedule 8Capital cost allowanceOnly with a buildingLand is not depreciable property. A building standing on it is, in Class 1, so Schedule 8 can apply in a year with no rent at all.

Source: the schedule requirements the Canada Revenue Agency sets for a T2 return, applied to a corporation holding real property that produced no income in the tax year. Last reviewed November 19, 2026.

settings.description_text: Land carries no capital cost allowance. A building on it does, which is why Schedule 8 can apply to a corporation with no tenant.

settings.title_text: Rent Makes It a Rental Corporation
settings.description_text: One month of rent on one unit is enough. That year is a full return rather than a nil one.
Property tax or insurance paid by the corporation is an expense on Schedule 125, and that ends the nil year.

settings.html:
The year is nil

  • No rent, lease payment or licence fee reached the corporation
  • No property tax, insurance or mortgage payment was made by it
  • No property, lot or interest in one was sold or transferred
  • No deposit, option fee or holding payment was received
  • No interest was credited on any account it holds

The year is not nil

  • Rent was collected for any part of the year, from any tenant
  • The corporation paid property tax, insurance or mortgage interest
  • Land, a building or part of one was sold or transferred out
  • An option fee or a deposit on a future sale was taken in
  • A development, servicing or survey cost was paid by the corporation

Due either way

  • A T2 for every tax year the corporation exists
  • A T183CORP signed by an authorised signing officer, per tax year
  • Schedule 8, for as long as a building stands on the land
  • The provincial land registry record, which the T2 does not touch
  • A clearance certificate, before the property can be distributed out

settings.title: Property Holding Corporation Filing Across Canada

settings.editor:
Real estate holding corporations are filed the same way wherever the registered office sits, because the return is prepared and transmitted electronically from end to end. There is nothing to print, nothing to post and nothing to sign in person.

Where the corporation was incorporated changes the registry, not the return. An Ontario corporation answers to the Ontario Business Registry, and corporations in British Columbia, Alberta, Quebec and Saskatchewan each answer to their own. The T2 itself is federal and identical in all of them. Within Ontario, a corporation registered in Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton or Ottawa is filed on the same terms and at the same price as one anywhere else in the country.

Two provinces add a return the federal T2 does not cover. A Quebec corporation also files the CO-17 and an Alberta corporation also files the AT1. Both are separate provincial returns, and neither is included in the $300.00 plus HST fee.

items.item_title: My corporation owns a rental property. Is any year nil?
We bought a lot and have not built on it. Is that nil?
I pay the property tax personally. Does that help?
Does the corporation file Schedule 8 with no rent?
We sold the property last year. What does that year look like?
A buyer paid a deposit we later returned. Is the year nil?
My spouse and I hold it together. Who is listed?
Can I transfer the property out and then dissolve?
Does the land registry filing count as the corporate return?
How many idle years can be filed together?

settings.editor: Not a year it collected rent. A corporation receiving rent is a rental corporation for that year and files a full T2. A year before the first tenant, or after the last one left with nothing paid or received, can be nil.
It can be, provided the corporation itself neither received nor paid anything during the year. Land sitting still earns nothing, so the usual obstacle is property tax rather than income.
It can. A cost a shareholder pays personally is not the corporation’s expense. What decides it is which entity paid, and the bank record is what shows that.
Where a building stands on the land, yes. A building is depreciable property in Class 1 whether or not it earned. Bare land is not depreciable and carries no Schedule 8.
A full return. A disposition puts a capital gain or loss in the year, and any recapture on a building goes with it, so that year is not nil.
No. The deposit moving in and out is money through the corporation, so the year is active even though nothing was kept.
Each shareholder at 10% or more of a class is named on Schedule 50, whatever the split, and one authorised signing officer signs the T183CORP.
The transfer is a disposition in its own year, and a clearance certificate will not be issued while any year is unfiled. The outstanding returns come first.
No. The registry records title and the T2 reports the tax year. Neither one does the other’s job.
All of them. One T2 and one T183CORP per year, each at $300.00 plus HST per tax year, sent earliest first so the property cost base carries forward.
